title: Contextual Runbook Composer & Safe-Invoke Gateway
creator: Asha Menon
description: Problem: on-call engineers often need curated, context-aware runbook steps rather than one-size-fits-all playbooks. Current playbooks are stored as static fragments and require manual parameterization and verification before executing. Goal: deliver a service that composes runbook steps dynamically from incident context and exposes a Safe-Invoke Gateway that enforces RBAC, idempotency, dry-run, and rich audit telemetry. The composer should support parameter templates, conditional branching, and preflight validation. The Safe-Invoke Gateway will serve the Console, the admin SDK, and automation hooks (webhooks/alerts) and provide deterministic safety checks before any action that can change production state. Non-goals: a full authoring UI (we will integrate with existing snippet registry for v1), building a new KV cache store (use existing runtime cache), or replacing existing incident triage flows in week 1.
acceptance_criteria: Composer API can generate an ordered list of steps from incident context and template snippets
Safe-Invoke API validates caller identity, enforces RBAC, supports dry-run, and returns an auditable invocation ID
Idempotency: duplicate invocations with same idempotency key are recognized and not re-executed
Execution records are emitted to audit-log with full parameter diffs and telemetry tags
Unit tests + integration tests for composition, validation, and RBAC pass in CI
Latency: composition endpoint P95 < 120ms under normal load (10 req/s)
work_log: 2026-03-03: Spike completed comparing composition strategies. Chose deterministic template expansion + simple rules engine (no full scripting) to reduce blast radius.
2026-03-05: PoC composer returns hydrated step list. Decided to store templates in existing snippet registry (no new storage service).

2026-03-08: Designed idempotency scheme: caller-provided idempotency_key + SHA256(prefix+params) stored in composer-memory-cache for 24h. Edge-case: long running actions may need extended retention - tracked.
2026-03-09: Security review kickoff. Primary concerns: parameter injection, privilege escalation via template variables. Added static variable allowlist and runtime validator.
2026-03-12: Integration tests flaky when parallel invocations race on cache eviction. Mitigation: add optimistic locking on invocation IDs and move critical section to gateway service.
2026-03-15: Draft API contract posted for review (see links). Began wiring Console callsite and admin-sdk helper.
2026-03-16: Ready for cross-team review. Need final sign-off on RBAC policy mapping and telemetry tag schema.
notes: Rollout plan: feature-flagged gateway. Phase 1: console + CLI dry-run and audit only. Phase 2: limited exec for SRE on-call rotation. Phase 3: broader team access after 2 weeks of stable telemetry.
Monitoring: emit invocation.created, invocation.validated, invocation.executed, invocation.failed. Create Grafana dashboard with invocation error-rate, validation-failures, and RBAC-deny counts.
Trade-offs: opted for deterministic template expansion (low flexibility) to avoid embedding Turing-complete logic; future iterations can add sandboxed scripting if necessary.
Rollback: disable execution route via feature flag; preserve auditing for post-mortem. If idempotency collisions observed, revert new idempotency-key namespace prefix to older format.
Open questions: retention period for invocation records (60d vs 365d), and whether to add HSM-backed signing for invocation IDs for non-repudiation.
